stem.en: The risk and return graph places fixed deposits low, mutual funds further along, and shares furthest, where both risk and possible return are highest. Which statement follows from that placement?

text.en: An investment with a higher possible return is guaranteed to earn more than a fixed deposit over any period.
An investment with a higher possible return also carries a higher chance of loss, because the two move together.
An investment with a higher possible return has more liquidity, since higher returns always come with easier access.
An investment with a higher possible return carries less risk, because the higher return pays for the extra risk.

explanation.en: The rising line shows a trade-off: a higher return is possible only when results can vary a lot, and that includes losing money. It is not a guarantee of more in every period, and it says nothing about liquidity.

hints.en: Read the line as a set of choices, not as a set of promises. What has to be accepted at the right-hand end of it?
Liquidity is a separate factor. Does the line say anything about how quickly an option turns into cash when you sell it?
